text:
Alex: Quick sweep notes for the new "turing-8b" candidate (fp16 vs int6). Dropping raw results + a suggested rollout for GTN.

Priya: please add artifact link and a one-line summary

Alex: artifacts: https://internal.storage/runs/1768504321/turing8b-sweep.tar.gz

Alex: One-line: int6 gives ~2.4x token-cost reduction, median latency +10-14ms, p95 increases a bit on long contexts; most QA/chat slices lose ~1-2% absolute, but a safety/rare-entity slice shows ~5% recall drop.

Priya: Abridged numbers (from the sweep):

```
model: turing-8b
mode: fp16  /  int6
median: 50ms   /  62ms
p95: 120ms    /  135ms
throughput (tok/s): 200 / 480
cost/token: $0.00090 / $0.00037
qa-f1: 0.915 / 0.901 (-1.5%)
rare-entity-recall: 0.80 / 0.76 (-5.0%)
```

Jordan: For GTN the economics look compelling, but product will be sensitive to any regressions that hit search/knowledge assistants. How widespread is the rare-entity slice?

Priya: Rare-entity ~2.8% of total traffic, concentrated in Knowledge and Search. Standard chat queries see <0.6%.

Kaia: Infra observations: int6 runs show higher peak qps (good), but slightly more KV-cache misses at 24k contexts which can nudge the p95 under heavy load. Memory footprint OK.

Dev-bot: perf-ci: job 1768504321 finished 4 smoke checks OK, 2 eval regressions flagged (rare-entity), logs -> /ci/1768504321/logs

Sam: Is the rare-entity drop user-visible or just metric-level? What does it mean for task success rate?

Priya: Manually checked a set of production prompts: mostly fine, but recall loss leads to missing facts in ~0.06% of total traffic; hits a few customers noticeably more.

Alex: Proposed rollout for GTN beta:
- Canary 10% of non-critical traffic for 72h
- Whitelist: exclude CoreSearch and legal/finance assistants
- Monitor metrics: slice-level recall, hallucination heuristics, task-success proxies
- Auto-fallback to fp16 if: >3% relative drop on core slices OR >0.8% absolute increase in task-failure proxy
- Enable KV-cache warmup during canary

Jordan: +1 but product wants the whitelist formalized and a pre-approved customer opt-in for the canary

Kaia: I'll add autoscale caps and a per-session concurrency limit for canary. Also enable KV warmup flag to keep tails down.

Priya: Ops ask: run the safety/adversarial suite before external customers. We should gate on that result.

Alex: Agreed. If adversarial sweep is clean we can default int6 for GTN beta with per-customer rollback; otherwise we'll iterate quant params.

Security: Acknowledged. We'll run a 300-sample adversarial set overnight and post findings.

Alex: Cost impact ask: what's delta for a mid-tier GTN customer at 100M tokens/mo?

Priya: Quick calc: fp16 @ $0.00090/tok -> $90k/mo. int6 @ $0.00037/tok -> $37k/mo. Savings ~ $53k/mo (~59% lower raw token cost), pre-batching/caching.

Jordan: That's a strong economic win for GTN acquisition. Product will draft risk comms and opt-in terms.

Alex: I'll create the canary flag, small eval harness for the safety prompts, and post a short playbook once CI artifacts are stable. Tagging @Product for whitelist and @Security for the adversarial pass.

Kaia: :thumbsup: autoscaling limits and KV warmup enabled for canary

Dev-bot: canary-deploy created at 1768504367 b link: https://deploys.internal/canary/1768504367

Alex: Timeline note: canary start 2026-04-03 16:00 UTC, monitoring window 72h. Will report verdict after the window.

Priya: Also adding a short checklist: 1) adversarial suite run 2) targeted customer whitelist 3) fallback toggle verified 4) safeties monitored

Sam: If we see only metric-level regressions but no task-failure signals, are we OK to proceed? Need product input.

Jordan: Product: if task-failure remains negligible and regressions are isolated to rare slices, we can proceed but limit initial rollout and include an explicit rollback and SLA clause.

Alex: OK thanks all. I'll update this thread with the safety-run summary and the canary monitoring dashboard link once live. :rocket:
